title: Ports & Protocols Every Analyst Must Memorize
description: Your essential cheat sheet for triage.

slides.title: Ports: The Apartment Numbers 🚪
slides.content:
# IP Address = Street Address. Port = Apartment Number.

A single server has one IP address (e.g., `192.168.1.10`) but runs many services: Web, Email, SSH.

**Ports** tell the data which service to go to.

*   Port **80**: Web Server (HTTP)
*   Port **443**: Secure Web Server (HTTPS)
*   Port **22**: Remote Shell (SSH)

**Why you MUST memorize these:** As a Tier 1 analyst, you have **seconds** to decide if an alert is weird.
*   *Alert:* Outbound connection on **Port 21**. *(FTP - File Transfer)*. Is that normal in your environment? Maybe not.
*   *Alert:* Inbound connection on **Port 3389** from China. *(RDP - Remote Desktop)*. **HIGH PRIORITY ALERT.**

slides.title: The Critical Ports List (Print This!) 🖨️
slides.content: Memorize these 20 ports for your first day in the SOC.
slides.codeSnippet:
21  - FTP (File Transfer - Clear text password!) 🚨
22  - SSH (Secure Shell - Encrypted Admin Access)
23  - Telnet (Clear text remote access - NEVER USE) 🚨
25  - SMTP (Email Sending)
53  - DNS (Domain Name Resolution)
80  - HTTP (Unencrypted Web)
88  - Kerberos (Windows Authentication)
110 - POP3 (Email Retrieval - Clear text)
123 - NTP (Time Sync)
137-139 - NetBIOS (Old Windows File Sharing)
143 - IMAP (Email Retrieval)
161 - SNMP (Network Management - Often misconfigured) 🚨
389 - LDAP (Directory Services)
443 - HTTPS (Encrypted Web)
445 - SMB (Modern Windows File Sharing / Ransomware's favorite) 🚨
514 - Syslog
1433 - MS-SQL (Database)
3306 - MySQL (Database)
3389 - RDP (Remote Desktop) 🚨
8080 - HTTP Proxy / Alt Web

quizData.question: You see massive outbound traffic from a workstation to a strange IP address on port **445**. What is the immediate concern?

options.text: Ransomware is spreading or data is being stolen via Windows File Sharing.

quizData.explanation: Port 445 is SMB (Server Message Block), used by Windows for file sharing. Attackers use it for lateral movement and ransomware propagation.

slides.title: The Danger of RDP (Port 3389) 🚨
slides.content:
# The SOC Nightmare

**RDP (Remote Desktop Protocol)** allows someone to see and control a Windows computer screen remotely.

**Why it's dangerous:**
*   If an attacker steals a user's password, they can use RDP to log into that user's PC **as if they were sitting at the desk**.
*   **Exposed RDP:** Port 3389 open to the **entire internet** is like leaving your front door unlocked with a sign saying "Key under mat."

**SOC Analyst Action:** If you see **inbound** connections to port 3389 from **external IPs** (especially foreign countries), **ESCALATE IMMEDIATELY**. This is a top-tier incident.

slides.title: Ports and Malware C2 🦠
slides.content:
## Not Just Standard Ports

While you must know standard ports, advanced malware often uses **uncommon high ports** (e.g., `54321`, `4444`) or **mimics standard ports** (e.g., using port 443 to hide encrypted C2 traffic within normal HTTPS noise).

**This is why Layer 7 inspection (looking at the actual data) is critical.** Is it really HTTPS web traffic, or is it a Meterpreter reverse shell on port 443?
